medium: Pencil on a spiral-bound sketchbook page
provenance: Drawn by Larry from memory on 2026-09-05, the day of the photograph-by-photograph sitting. His son photographed the page in the sketchbook the same afternoon (phone photograph, file timestamp 13:31) and sent it to the archive; the sheet stays with the family. He offered to draw the three sheets himself; his son had not raised it. His son listened while he drew and did not take notes; nothing he said at this sheet has been recorded.
title: “Nui Ba Den”
description: A plan drawn in pencil on a sketchbook page, photographed with the spiral binding at the top. The words NUI BA DEN sit near the centre. Near the top edge is a box labelled FORT, with two smaller boxes drawn against the binding above it. To the left, the word GENERATORS is written above a rectangle enclosing a row of small arches. A long curved line sweeps from the top-left of the page down the left side, around the bottom, and up the right, enclosing most of the drawing; short lines at the upper left branch from it. In the lower centre a rounded shape is labelled HELI PAD, with several straight lines fanning downward from it toward the bottom edge. Right of centre is a small unlabelled box, and in the bottom-left corner a scribbled mark. Nothing on the sheet indicates scale, compass direction, or the slope.
researchNotes: Two of the four labels are things he has already put on the mountain in words: the French fort at his radio position (VN-0009, 'the stone is the french fort, my radio was outside') and the helicopter pad where the trees were being felled (VN-0157). Generators had not been mentioned before this sheet; they are new testimony. The unlabelled box and the mark in the bottom-left corner are not interpreted here.
